data.long_meaning: In Latin, Damiana means 'reaper of gentle reeds'. in_greek.name: Δαμιανά
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Δαμιανά προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη δαμ-, που σημαίνει να ακολουθώ ή να υπηρετώ. Είναι συνδεδεμένο με τη λέξη δήμος, που σημαίνει λαός ή πλήθος. Στην χριστιανική παράδοση, το όνομα Δαμιανά αναφέρεται σε μια γυναίκα που υπηρετεί ή βοηθά την κοινότητα ή τον λαό του Θεού.

data.cultural_impact: Although there isn't a direct cultural significance to the name "Damiana" in Christianity, it can be linked to the precious Damian saints who had a tremendous impact on society, particularly in the fields of healthcare and charity. Damian of Moloka'i, known as the "Prince of Martyrs," served as a priest and a physician on the Hawaiian island of Moloka'i, caring for the lepers who were shunned by society. Meanwhile, Damian of Antioch, along with his brother Cosmas, were Roman soldiers who were executed for refusing to deny their Christian faith during the Roman Empire. Both saints lived noble lives, showing compassion and courage, inspiring generations of admirers through their unwavering dedication to their faith and service to others.
